close_reason: Fixed in bf895d2: added rustdoc to ContactCard documenting that ::default() produces a partial card for incremental construction, not a valid wire payload — the handler layer (jmap-contacts-server) rejects partial cards on /set create. Matches the workspace pattern: Email, Task, CalendarEvent all derive Default for the same partial-construction use case. Removing the Default derive would diverge from the sibling pattern and break common usage.
description:
ContactCard derives `Default` (card.rs:31). The derived default sets
all 22+ optional fields to None.

```rust
let c = ContactCard::default();
let wire = serde_json::to_string(&c).unwrap();
// wire == "{}"
```

A wire ContactCard is not valid without:
- `id`: required JMAP addition (RFC 9610 §3)
- `addressBookIds`: required JMAP addition (RFC 9610 §3, server-side)

A server crate that does:

```rust
let mut card = ContactCard::default();
card.uid = Some("urn:uuid:...".into());
// forgot to set id, addressBookIds
return Ok(card);  // serializes to {"uid": "urn:uuid:..."}
```

…produces a wire payload that JMAP-strict clients will reject as
"missing required fields".

`#[non_exhaustive]` prevents struct-literal construction from outside
the crate, so callers cannot do
`ContactCard { uid: ..., ..Default::default() }`.
But `ContactCard::default()` itself is callable, so a caller can
construct a default and patch fields one at a time.

Additional immutability concern: once `Default` is shipped in 0.x.y, it
is a forever-promise. Removing it is a breaking change. If the crate
later adopts a typestate builder pattern that prevents wire-invalid
construction, `Default` cannot coexist with that.

Three resolutions:

1. Remove the `Default` derive entirely. Force callers to construct
   via `serde_json::from_value` or a future builder. Cost: tests inside
   this crate currently rely on `Default` for ergonomic struct init.
   Each test would need to switch to from_value-based construction
   (already the pattern in most tests; see lib.rs).

2. Keep `Default` but rename to `ContactCard::empty()` with a clear
   "this is not a wire-valid card" doc clause. Requires deprecating the
   Default impl.

3. Keep `Default` and add a doc clause explicitly stating the wire-
   invalidity and pointing callers at a future `try_into_wire_card()`
   validator.

Lowest-risk fix: option 3 (doc clause). Adds zero API surface; documents
the footgun. The doc clause should also note that the only correct way
to construct a wire-valid ContactCard from outside the crate today is
via `serde_json::from_value` or `from_str` against a JSON literal
containing `id` and `addressBookIds`.

Same analysis applies to `AddressBook::default()` — but AddressBook
does NOT derive Default (addressbook.rs:45-46 only has
`#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]`). Verify
this asymmetry is intentional and document the rationale.

Same analysis applies to `ContactCardFilterCondition::default()` — that
one IS valid empty (matches every card per RFC 9610 §3.3.1), so the
Default derive there is fine.
title: ContactCard::default() builds a wire-invalid card; serializing emits "{}"
